title: The Slop Drop
one_liner: Watch an AI 'bulk-solve' 722 math problems in real time, with a live meter of time, cost, and success rate.
speaker: Peter Diamandis / Alex
context: OpenAI released 722 math solutions in one GitHub drop, each costing ~3 hours of compute, with only 15-20% of attempted problems solved, sparking mathematician backlash.
demo: A grid of 722 tiles represents unsolved problems; press play and watch tiles flip to 'solved' one by one at a pace the user can speed up, with running counters for elapsed compute-hours, estimated dollar cost, and % solved. A toggle lets the user compare 'human pace' (decades) vs 'AI pace' (two weeks) on a timeline.
data_plan: Bundled dataset built from stated podcast figures (722 problems, ~3 hrs/problem, 15-20% solve rate, low-tens-of-millions cost estimate, 'decade of progress in a week' claim); grid-fill animation is simulated.
risks: Must clearly label the solve animation as a stylized simulation using the podcast's stated figures, not a reproduction of OpenAI's actual released proofs.

episode.title: OpenAI Bulk-Solves 722 Math Problems, Anthropic’s Cruelty Policy, and Elon’s Quadrillion-Dollar SpaceX | EP #302
